name: Talaud Bush-hen
rangeDescription: Talaud islands (northern moluccas)
description: A large, entirely dark, pale-billed rail confined to the Talaud Archipelago. Upperparts and head dark brown, underparts completely slate-colored.

name: Kadavu Fantail
rangeDescription: Kadavu (fiji)
description: Mouse-brown above and white below. Head brown with a white throat above a variable black band.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Black-chinned Mountain Tanager
rangeDescription: Humid andes of western colombia and western ecuador
description: Large and colorful tanager of Andean cloud forest in western Ecuador and western Colombia. Plumage is golden-yellow with a black head, blue wing patch, and yellow stripe on rear crown.

name: Pale-throated Pampa-Finch
rangeDescription: Locally on serras of eastern brazil (interior central bahia and minas gerais)
description: Large finch with a long spiky tail. Mostly gray with olive-green wings and tail.

name: Gosling's Bunting
rangeDescription: Southern mauritania to southern senegal, eastward to southeastern chad, northeastern central african republic, southwestern sudan, and northwestern south sudan; possibly also far northeastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A bunting with cinnamon underparts, black-and-brown mottled upperparts, and a black-and-orange bill. The male’s head is boldly striped black-and-white and the throat is pale gray.

name: Giant Kingbird
rangeDescription: Cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; off southwestern cuba); formerly great inagua and caicos islands
description: A large flycatcher typically found singly or in pairs hunting from upper branches in wooded areas. It is grayish above and whitish below with a blackish crown and face, which resembles Eastern, Gray and Loggerhead Kingbirds, but none have the truly massive bill of the Giant Kingbird.

name: Streak-breasted Treehunter
rangeDescription: Central highlands of costa rica and western panama
description: This warm brown forest dweller is similar to many other foliage-gleaners and treehunters. Look for the relatively bright orangey throat with streaking on the breast.

name: Chilean Hawk
rangeDescription: Andes of central chile and argentina to tierra del fuego
description: Uncommon and elusive hawk of Patagonian forest in central and southern Chile and neighboring parts of Argentina. Adult is mostly gray with darker crown and upperparts; underparts are mottled or barred with white and chestnut.

name: Yellow-winged Cacique
rangeDescription: Pacific lowlands of western mexico (southeastern sonora) to southeastern guatemala
description: Spectacular and conspicuous black-and-yellow bird of tropical lowlands in west Mexico. Favors deciduous forest and edges, plantations, and hedges with tall trees; often in towns and villages, especially near streams and rivers.

name: Purple Grenadier
rangeDescription: Southeastern south sudan, southern ethiopia, somalia, northeastern uganda, kenya, and tanzania
description: A distinctive and attractive waxbill with a deep-blue tail and a red bill. Males are more colorful, with a purple belly, a rufous hood, and purple and red around the eye.

name: Cloven-feathered Dove
rangeDescription: New caledonia and île des pins
description: Unique and spectacular large dove with a weird shape: fat with a short tail and lumpy head. Male bright green with a yellow belly and very long, even brighter yellow undertail coverts that nearly reach the tip of the tail.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Pink-footed Shearwater
rangeDescription: Mocha and juan fernández islands off chile; ranges to north pacific
description: Large shearwater, often messy-looking with smudgy brown neck and underwings. Underparts are usually fairly clean white, but sometimes mottled brownish or rarely all-dark.

name: Red-billed Woodcreeper
rangeDescription: Southeastern venezuela to the guianas and brazil north of the amazon river
description: Large, stout-billed woodcreeper of tall rainforest in northeastern Amazonia. Plumage entirely rufous-brown with no barring or streaking; note thick reddish bill, white throat, and prominent white whisker mark (bill of young birds is dark brown).

name: European Honey-buzzard
rangeDescription: Western palearctic; winters southern europe and iran to southern africa
description: Lanky raptor with a slender head and long wings with prominent “fingers.” Plumage is highly variable, but note tail pattern: pale overall with a dark tip, and two wide-spaced narrow dark bars on the basal half. Compare with the much stockier Common Buzzard, which has a shorter neck, more rounded wings, and steadier wingbeats.

name: Caracas Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Coastal mountains of northern venezuela (aragua, miranda, and distrito federal)
description: Boldly patterned sparrow with black head and white eyebrow. Back and tail olive-yellow, underparts white; black band across chest.

name: Palau Swiftlet
rangeDescription: Lowlands of palau (western caroline islands)
description: A small, mostly uniformly light brown swiftlet with a slightly darker cap, a cinnamon-tinged throat, and a lightly forked tail. Occurs on larger islands, especially over highland ridges and gorges.

name: White-fronted Falconet
rangeDescription: Forest of northern borneo
description: Tiny, compact, black-and-white falcon. Black above, with a white chest and pale orangish belly.

name: Luzon Flameback
rangeDescription: Northern philippines (luzon, polillo, catanduanes, and marinduque)
description: A large woodpecker of lowland and foothill wooded areas on Luzon and neighboring islands, with a red back, a yellowish belly with indistinct patterning, and black on the tail, edge to the wing, neck, and chest. Note the obvious white spotting on the chest, neck, and line behind the eye.

name: Forster's Tern
rangeDescription: North america; winters southern usa to costa rica and greater antilles
description: Smaller than all the gulls, with thinner and more pointed bill. Distinguished from other terns by pale whitish wings and orange-based bill in summer, and isolated black ear patch in winter.

name: Elegant Tern
rangeDescription: Southern california to western mexico (nayarit); winters guatemala to chile
description: Long-billed tern of the Pacific coast, from the U.S. to Chile.
